tossups.text: In this work, African-Americans are referred to as "Children of Ham," and one character discovers the main character's diary with Professor Knotly Wade. That character, Professor Pieixoto, refers to one entity in this work as the "Underground Frailroad." Born Eurydice, the protagonist has a relationship with Nick and plays Scrabble with her boss, whose wife Serena Joy is jealous of the protagonist's fertility. Set in the military dictatorship of Gilead, this novel is narrated by the Commander's concubine Offred. For 10 points, name this novel by Margaret Atwood.

When given an electron density for a 1-electron system, this quantity is described by the von Weizsacker functional. Two times the average value of this equals a constant times the average of its counterpart by the virial theorem. One can use the virial theorem to derive the equipartition theorem, which gives that this quantity is three-halves times the Boltzmann constant times temperature. This quantity is equal to momentum squared over two times mass. The rotational form of this is equal to one-half times the moment of inertia times the angular velocity squared. Name this quantity which, in translational motion, equals one-half times mass times velocity squared.

In human physiology, this structure is essential for insulin and glucagon. It plays a key role in the endocrine system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this insulin-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The insulin is a key component of the Endocrine system, involved in insulin and glucagon.

tossups.text: They're not from Brazil, but Arthania and Kuyaba were two of the three realms the lands of these people were divided into by Arab authors. Some scholars have postulated a controversial hypothetical state of these people based on use of the word "chacanus" ("hah-kah-nooss") in texts like the Annales Bertiniani. A controversial document may reference a king of these people when using the letters HLGW. Modern nationalists who claim that these people were almost entirely autochthonous are called anti-Normanists. The founder of a dynasty of these people was "called" to rule a city known to a people to their west as Holmgard. They aren't Bulgars, but the hygiene of these people was criticized by Aḥmad ibn Faḍlān. An elite bodyguard unit for Byzantine emperors was named these people, the Varangian Guard. For 10 points, name these people who founded a state governed from Kyiv.

This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for epidermis structure. It plays a key role in the integumentary system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this epidermis-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The epidermis is a key component of the Integumentary system, involved in epidermis structure.

tossups.text: To protect Bindusara from poison, Chanakya performed this action and subsequently placed Bindusara inside the stomachs of goats for seven days. This action was performed on a dying Clothru at Lough ("lock") Ree, where her son Furbaide later avenged her by slinging cheese at Medb ("mayve"). After Coronis's ill-fated affair with Ischys, Apollo performed this action at her funeral pyre, earning Aesclepius his name. To aid Rudaba, Zal burned a white feather to summon the Simurgh and received its guidance on how to perform this action using wine. This action likely was not performed on Aurelia Cotta, as she survived to see her son invade Britain. For 10 points, despite a misinterpretation of Pliny the Elder, what obstetrical procedure is not actually named for the birth of Rome's dictator for life?
acceptableAnswers: prompt on answers that indicate cutting someone open by asking “for what specific procedure?”

tossups.text: A memory management unit translates addresses described by this adjective to their physical locations. Paging can be used with memory described by this adjective. It's not "guest" or "host," but a hypervisor supervises these types of machines, which can be used to emulate Windows on other devices. Java byte code is executed on a machine described by this adjective. A paradigm described by this adjective can be experienced using the HTC Vive device. For 10 points, name this word that describes a type of "reality" offered by the Oculus Rift.

A cultural account of the English form of this concept was provided by Marilyn Strathernn in her book After Nature. David Murray Schneider launched a "project" studying this concept among the lower-middle class in the United States and Great Britain. Harrison White introduced abstract algebra into the study of this concept in his monograph An Anatomy of it. Locating the "atom" of this concept is the goal of the "alliance theory" approach for studying it. The Crow, Iroquois, Sudanese, and Hawaiian patterns of terminology for this subject are among the six identified by Lewis Henry Morgan. Many Western Pacific cultures use "dyadic terms" when talking about this phenomenon. "Fictive" forms of this phenomenon are based neither on affinal nor consanguineal ties. Claude Levi-Strauss wrote a book about the "elementary structures" of this phenomenon. For 10 points, name this term denoting the social relationships between people in societies.

A Wolfgang Borchert story titled for this object concerns a woman who lies in agreement with her husband that "something was there." Phrases like "Isn't that" and "Think it is" are repeated in bizarre rhythms in a David Ives play in which "Philip Glass Buys [one of these objects]." The title object of Lu Xun's "Medicine" is one of these objects dripping with the blood of an executed revolutionary. Rosencrantz and Guildenstern often recite a quote in which this object is replaced by "mask", "week," "round," or "cue." Ivan Denisovich sews parts of these objects inside his mattress. "An obscure reference in Maimonides" lets a pitiful man who makes these objects return to his wife Elka after he accuses her of adultery due to her sons born out of wedlock. Years later, Elka admits to having other men's children, leading a "Spirit of Evil" to convince her husband to put his urine in these objects. A Gogol story begins with Ivan finding a nose inside one of these objects, which are baked by Gimpel the Fool. For 10 points, what foodstuff was paired with a "jug of wine" by Omar Khayyam?

The Beveridge Curve compares this economic concept with the number of job vacancies. Okun's Law notes that GDP will decrease by 2% if this rate increases by 1%. It can be explained by seasonal lulls in demand or, in its "frictional" type, by naturally occurring transitions in the economy. The "99ers" are long-term sufferers of this phenomenon, which increases during recessions. For 10 points, give this term for people lacking work.

Mortensen used Search and Matching Theory to model one form of this phenomenon, while external expectations create multiple equilibrium points for it according to Peter Diamond's Coconut Model. The Shapiro-Stiglitz model implies that efficiency wages sustain this phenomenon, which is similarly maintained according to the NAIRU model developed by Phelps and Friedman. Okun's law posits the inverse relationship between this and GDP, while the Beveridge Curve is particularly useful in modeling a type of this phenomenon created by mismatched conditions, its "frictional" form. The Phillips Curve plots inflation against, for 10 points, what economic phenomenon in which laborers are out of work?
acceptableAnswers: do NOT accept more general answers like "poverty"

tossups.text: A character in this musical sings "Whenever I see someone less fortunate than I ... / My tender heart starts to bleed". This musical's protagonist leaves with Fiyero after singing "For Good" with a character who gave them a makeover in "Popular". This musical's number "Defying Gravity" sees the protagonist enchant a broom to go to Emerald City to confront the Wizard. For 10 points, name this musical about Glinda and Elphaba, two witches in Oz.

The F major second movement of this symphony begins with the muted first violins slowly and quietly playing "F [pause] low C, long A [pause] G, F, E," to which the other muted strings respond with a forte staccato eighth-note chord. This symphony's final movement features a theme that had earlier been used in its composer's F major Missa brevis. Unison C, twice followed by triplet sixteenth-notes back up to C, opens this symphony's first movement, which quotes its composer's aria "Un bacio di mano." The four-note theme "C, D, F, E" appears in this 1788 symphony's final movement, which closes with a five-voice fugato. The "Great G minor" symphony immediately preceded, for 10 points, what last symphony by Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart that was nicknamed for a Roman god?

In this short story, Judith Cardenier unknowingly tells her father that his wife "broke a blood-vessel" while arguing with a peddler while the title man was away with the "crew of the Half-moon." A sound "like distant peals of thunder" in this story is actually a group of ghosts playing ninepins, who keep the title man away from his home during the American Revolution. For 10 points, name this Washington Irving short story in which the title Dutch villager falls asleep for twenty years.

The Bano case was brought by victims of this event, which is memorialized by a statue of a mother holding a child and one hand to her face. Arthur Little's report about this incident suggested it was an act of sabotage, and a yearly protest about this event burns an effigy of Warren Anderson on its anniversary. A fake spokesman named "Jude Finsterra", actually the prankster Andy Bichlbaum of the Yes Men, stated that the company involved would set up a 12 billion dollar fund for the victims of this disaster. This event was caused by the backflow of water into a tank used to store the product of phosgene and methylamine from a plant that made pesticide. This disaster resulted in several thousand deaths by suffocation and circulatory collapse as the cloud of chemicals blew southwards. For 10 points, name this 1984 industrial disaster in Madhya Pradesh in which methyl isocyanate gas leaked from a Union Carbide plant.

"Full stack" developers can program these things by working both with the front end and back end. HTML, CSS, and JavaScript are commonly used to program these things. Some of these things save information about visiting users with the use of cookies. These things can be accessed by computers using an IP address or a URL. For 10 points, name these things which consist of collections of web pages, such as google.com.

this structure is essential for t cells and cell-mediated immunity. It plays a key role in the immune system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this T cell-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The T cell is a key component of the Immune system, involved in t cells and cell-mediated immunity.

tossups.text: A tension between this principle and individual freedom was illustrated with an example involving the characters "Lewd" and "Prude" who disagree about what to do with a copy of Lady Chatterley's Lover. Amartya Sen proved there is no social choice function which satisfies this property and also allows more than one individual to be decisive over a pair of alternatives, a result called the "liberal paradox." Arrow's impossibility theorem shows that there's no non-dictatorial social welfare function satisfying universal domain, IIA (eye-eye-A), and this property. Every competitive equilibrium has this property according to the first theorem of welfare economics. For 10 points, identify this condition where it is impossible to make one party better off without making someone worse off.

In a novel from this country, Maureen runs towards an unknown helicopter after fleeing to the title servant's village in July's People. The activist Arthur Jarvis is murdered in a novel from this country, causing Stephen Kumalo to be summoned to its capital. Long Walk to Freedom is the autobiography of a political leader from this nation. Cry, the Beloved Country is a novel from this country, which is the home of the authors Nadine Gordimer and Alan Paton. For 10 points, name this home country of Nelson Mandela, whose literature sometimes focuses on issues of apartheid.

In this city, two weeks after the Battle of Gettysburg, riots broke out against a new draft law. A 1969 police raid against a gay club in this city led to the Stonewall riots. This city was led by Ed Koch in the 1980s and was controlled by Boss Tweed's Tammany Hall in the 19th century. Its other mayors include Rudy Giuliani, who gained fame for his response when this city's World Trade Center was attacked. For 10 points, name this largest city in the U.S.

parts.text: Name this character who is "in England" in an Elizabeth Bishop poem. This character created by Daniel Defoe converts the cannibal Friday to Christianity after he reaches the "Island of Despair."
This poet described "Children picking up our bones" at the beginning of "A Postcard from the Volcano," a poem collected in the "Ideas of Order" section of his collection Harmonium.

This poet referred to Mount Rainier as "the white volcano with no weather side" in the poem "An Octopus." The speaker of a different poem by this author hopes the "autocrats among us can be 'literalists of the imagination'" and present "imaginary gardens with real toads in them."

bonuses.leadin: In a poem from the perspective of this character, he describes "fifty-two miserable, small volcanoes I could climb," one of which he names Mount Despair. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This Londoner's 1529 tract Supplication of the Beggars denounced the unreformed clergy for their greed, luxury, and lechery.
John Penry was executed in 1593 for his role in the production of the texts circulated under this pen name. They were vicious satires against bishops produced by a secret printing press.
Anticlerical supporters of "further reformation" had their final victory with the 1645 execution of this man, who served as Archbishop of Canterbury under Charles I.

bonuses.leadin: Name these figures associated with anticlericalism in the English Reformation, For 10 points each.

What is the main function of the contraction in the musculoskeletal system?
Name another component of the musculoskeletal system related to sliding filament theory.

parts.text: Name this herald of the Greek forces during the Trojan War. In the Iliad, Hera likens herself to this character as she speaks with the voice of "fifty men" to the Greeks, shaming them for fleeing the field of battle.
Unfortunately, Stentor's voice did not give him the super strength he needed to defeat this god in a shouting contest, so Stentor's lungs burst from exhaustion. This god carried the caduceus staff.

This god took a lot of credit for the gods' victory in the Titanomachy because his great shout frightened the Titans. He lends his name to a type of fear, which he caused by shouting loudly after being awoken from naps.

bonuses.leadin: In the Politics, Aristotle asks "who shall serve as herald" if there is nobody with the "lungs" of this character, to give an example of why an effective state must have a minimum number of people. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this atmospheric region in the upper stratosphere, consisting of a gas built of oxygen atoms that blocks most of the sun's ultraviolet radiation.
The ozone layer was found to be depleting in the 1970s mainly due to this family of industrial chemicals. Name this kind of compound which includes chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) and bromofluorocarbons.

The weakest possible bond between a carbon center and a halogen atom is intentionally added in the generic variety of this food additive. Name this halite mined from Pakistan whose unpurified state is its primary selling point.

bonuses.leadin: Humans are pretty good at ruining the environment. For 10 points,

parts.text: The Structural Transformation of the Public Sphere was written by this German philosopher. He distinguished between strategic action and action aimed at achieving understanding in The Theory of Communicative Action.
Habermas engaged in a series of debates with this French thinker who theorized deconstruction and wrote Of Grammatology.

bonuses.leadin: This work presents 18th and 19th-century cafés and salons as model environments for rational and critical discourse and the formation of public opinion. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Along with E. W. Johnson, this author edited a collection titled The New Journalism. He told the story of the Merry Pranksters in The Electric Kool-Aid Acid Test and also wrote a fictional book dramatizing "yuppie" angst titled The Bonfire of the Vanities.
Another author who used New Journalism was Hunter S. Thompson, who wrote a book about Raoul Duke going to this southwest city, where he encounters the title "fear and loathing."

One of the first pieces of New Journalism was a 1966 Esquire article by Gay Talese, profiling this man, who was said to have "a cold." Talese wrote a profile of this celebrity without ever actually interviewing him.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about the literary genre known as "New Journalism," which combined journalism with literary devices found in fictional works, for 10 points each.

parts.text: This is used instead of a period at the end of an interrogative sentence.
This is used in lists when the individual items already have commas and is also used to separate two independent clauses within a sentence.
This diacritical mark similar to a diaeresis or trema is used to shift German vowels.

bonuses.leadin: Identify these punctuation or diacritical marks, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name these people whose "discouraged" type, who number just under 400,000 in the U.S., are not included in a basic economic measure that equaled 3.5 percent in January 2023.
Mundell's fourth condition requires similarity in these things. Greg Mankiw (MAN-kyoo) critiqued the "real" theory of these things for overvaluing the impact of large technological shifts.
Mundell's criteria were not fully met by this common currency, introduced in countries such as Germany and France in 1999.

bonuses.leadin: Free movement of these people is among Robert Mundell's four conditions for an optimal currency region. For 10 points each:

parts.text: A major figure in the abstract expressionist movement, he originated the practice of action painting, as exemplified by his One: Number 31, 1950, and was once dubbed "the Dripper" by Time Magazine.
A leading figure in the pop art movement, this painter, filmmaker, illustrator, and author produced a portrait of Marilyn Monroe and designed some advertisement for Campbell's soup.
This printmaker produced a Map and some Numbers as well as lots of studies of the American flag, such as the one in which he drew three of them on top of each other.

bonuses.leadin: Name some crazy 20th century Americans who call themselves artists, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Identify this set of 15 violin suites for Archibishop Max Gandolph with a Biblical theme. Most of them are meditations on some aspect of Christ's life.
The Mystery Sonatas were composed by this man that is known for his stylus fantasticus composition style.
Heinrich Biber's stylus fantasticusi was the inspiration for this other composer's style. His own works include The Musical Offering and the St. Matthew Passion.

bonuses.leadin: The last one of these works is called "The Beatification of the Virgin" and ends with a sarabanda, while another one of these works is a 11 minute piece called "Pentecost." For 10 points each:

parts.text: This poet wrote of Chicago as a "hog butcher of the world, tool maker, stacker of wheat". He also said to "pile the bodies high at Austerlitz and Waterloo" in "Grass".
This Upton Sinclair novel goes over Jurgis Rudkis's struggle in the meat-packing industry of Chicago.
This author's The Song of The Lark is set in Chicago, which along with My Antonia and O Pioneers! is part of her "Nebraska Trilogy".

parts.text: Name this Pope who issued the Unam sanctam bull, declaring "every human creature" to be subject to the Pope's authority. In response, King Philip IV of France had this Pope arrested and beaten, leading to his death one month later.
Shortly after Boniface VIII's death, Clement V, an ally of King Philip, was elected Pope and moved the court from Rome to this French city.

Because of his debts to this group, Philip had Pope Clement summon the Council of Vienne to convict its members of heresy. Despite an acquittal, Pope Clement disbanded this order anyway and had its Grandmaster Jacques de Molay burned at the stake.

parts.text: Name that concept, exemplified by a participant in a game who elects to take $50 rather than flip a coin and take $101 for heads and $0 for tails.

For a single consumer, risk aversion is a concave curve in a plot of this function against the consumer's money. The "marginal" variety is the amount gained or lost from a step increase or decrease of consumption of a product.
This scientist presented the problem of risk aversion in his St. Petersburg Paradox. He names a utility function in which utility scales logarithmically, rather than linearly, with increasing wealth.

bonuses.leadin: Answer some questions about a concept that's inconsistent with classical economic models, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Herrick's poem is in this poetic genre, whose name means "seize the day."
The poem uses this literary device, which assigns human qualities to non-human things like time and the sun.
"To the Virgins, to Make Much of Time" is a sixteen-line poem composed of four of these four-line stanzas.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about Robert Herrick's poem "To the Virgins, to Make Much of Time," for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this Middle Eastern country. American forces supported this occupied country during the First Gulf War.
Kuwait's oil infrastructure was heavily damaged in the First Gulf War after it was invaded by this neighboring country, which was led at the time by Saddam Hussein from Baghdad.

During the Gulf War, the US effort was largely staged from this southern neighbor of Kuwait. This largest country in the Middle East controls much of the region's shipping, as it is the only country with shorelines on both the Persian Gulf and the Red Sea.
